question: Did the risk of a motorist being killed per mile driven in NYC decline from 2013 to 2025? Make a chart and answer based on this crash data.

options.metric: Annual number of motorists killed in police-reported NYC crashes, summed from number_of_motorist_killed
options.denominator: None; an annual count, not a rate
options.reason: A direct annual fatality count is a clear description of the motorist deaths recorded in the crash file, even though it has no exposure denominator.
options.answer: This file cannot establish a per-mile decline; the annual count proxy was 110 motorists killed in 2013 and 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This crash file cannot determine whether motorist death risk per mile declined because miles driven are not recorded. This framing sums number_of_motorist_killed across dated police-reported NYC crash rows with an observed value for each calendar year; it records 110 deaths in 2013 and 81 in 2025, an annual count rather than a risk rate. The count is a defensible description of recorded fatality burden, but it leaves the exposure-adjusted per-mile question unanswered. The data check found 2,132,218 in-scope rows, with zero missing motorist-killed values and zero missing crash dates among them, so no selected rows were dropped for those reasons; each year spans Jan. 1-Dec. 31 and Jan. 1 accounts for about 0.17%-0.22% of rows, though boundary dates do not prove complete reporting.

options.metric: Sum of motorists killed per 1,000 police-reported NYC crash rows with a nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed, by crash year
options.denominator: Number of police-reported crash rows with nonmissing number_of_motorist_killed in that year, scaled to 1,000 crashes
options.reason: Scaling motorist deaths by reported crash rows adjusts the count for changes in the number of crashes, while remaining explicit that miles driven are unavailable.
options.answer: This file cannot establish a per-mile decline; motorists killed per 1,000 reported crashes were 0.540 in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This crash file cannot determine whether motorist death risk per mile declined because miles driven are not recorded. This framing divides the annual sum of number_of_motorist_killed by the number of dated police-reported NYC crash rows with an observed value, then scales to 1,000 crashes; the metric is 0.540 in 2013 and 0.947 in 2025. It is a defensible crash-based severity measure that adjusts for annual crash-row totals, but it leaves deaths per mile and the per-mile risk question unanswered. The data check found 2,132,218 in-scope rows, with zero missing motorist-killed values and zero missing crash dates among them, so no selected rows were dropped from either numerator or denominator; each year spans Jan. 1-Dec. 31 and Jan. 1 accounts for about 0.17%-0.22% of rows, though boundary dates do not prove complete reporting.
